Scenarios.Scenario: Open, restore, or switch an integrated-browser editor, with empty or populated recent history.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: setInput resolves the browser model, initializes navigation state, refreshes the recent list synchronously, lays out the editor, and awaits browser visibility. The new list work precedes completion of setInput; periodic screenshots remain off that initialization path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve or create the native browser view, position it, and update visibility through IBrowserViewService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing model/view initialization per uncached browser ID; layout and visibility calls per editor initialization or visibility change, not per recent URL.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same browser-model initialization, native-view creation, layout, and visibility calls occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Model initialization and the final visibility request are awaited; editor layout remains fire-and-forget.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Capture the native browser screenshot and encode the returned buffer for the placeholder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing one-second interval per pane with a resolved input, subject to the existing model/overlay checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The screenshot interval, capture operation, and base64 conversion are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs periodically after input setup, not as part of the added history refresh.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: History written by this implementation contains at most 10 distinct URLs. Each input initially displays at most 3 rows. One BrowserEditor pane is reused for different tabs within an editor group; inactive tabs are not independent recent-list renderers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The additional history read, list construction, and row updates are synchronous renderer work. Existing asynchronous model initialization and visibility operations retain their previous scheduling; the diff adds no collection-wide IPC fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: History reads use the existing initialized workspace-storage memory map, including a cheap missing-key result; JSON is reparsed on refresh. BrowserEditorInput caches its model and in-flight resolution, and the workbench/main-process services reuse models/views by ID. Recent lists are recreated on input replacement, with old input resources cleared.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the traced initialization path, memory-backed storage reads, 10-entry write cap, 3-row initial display, and unchanged native-browser boundaries.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings are supplied for constructing the bounded list; URL lengths and number of simultaneously instantiated editor groups vary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable regression established. The added UI construction is bounded and does not add native-view or storage-read boundary calls per history entry.

Scenarios.Scenario: Navigate from the address bar or a recent URL, including redirects and modifier-click background opening.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Normal navigation issues one browser loadURL request. Its navigation event now updates recent history and synchronously refreshes subscribed pane lists. Saving history does not await persistence. Modifier-click opens one browser editor through the existing resolver, which starts resolving its model in the background.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward the selected URL to Electron webContents.loadURL.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One loadURL operation per explicit navigation or newly opened recent-URL editor, not one per stored entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Address-bar navigation already used this loadURL IPC. The new recent-entry affordance reuses the same single-navigation path rather than multiplying requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The navigation promise awaits page loading; history recording occurs on the existing navigation event.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Electron loads the requested document, redirects, and its resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One requested page and its normal resource/redirect graph per user navigation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Navigating to the same URL through the address bar or existing editor-opening path performed the same network work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Document navigation and page loading determine navigation completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse and stringify the workspace recent-URL array.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Arrays contain at most 10 entries through the supplied writer. One save for addition and, only on a successful redirect removal, one preceding save; each subscribed pane reparses on its refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no recent-URL serialization or history-driven list refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small synchronous renderer work in navigation-event handling; it does not wait for disk.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist coalesced workspace-storage changes through the storage channel and a SQLite transaction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared storage update per flush batch, with one final recent-history key value and the target marker when needed; no per-URL database requests. Closely spaced changes replace the pending value for the same key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Workspace persistence already existed, but browser navigation did not enqueue this history key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Deferred and not awaited by addRecentUrl/removeRecentUrl, so persistence is off the navigation-event critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most 10 stored entries; one history addition per pending user navigation, plus a removal if a different original URL actually exists in history. Refresh fan-out is to subscribed BrowserEditor panes/editor groups, not all browser tabs or all URLs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: History mutations and event delivery are synchronous. Each mutation refreshes subscribed panes serially. Storage uses a 100 ms ThrottledDelayer and pending-key maps; remove/add within one redirect handler normally coalesce into one persistence batch. The diff adds no concurrent load for each history item.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Successful history additions deduplicate by exact URL before truncating to 10. Redirect removal misses do not write or emit. Workspace storage serves reads from memory, deduplicates unchanged values, and coalesces pending writes by key. Empty history requires no disk lookup on refresh.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in call counts, event fan-out granularity, capped history size, and deferred/coalesced storage persistence.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact URL byte lengths, navigation frequency, and number of subscribed editor-group panes vary; no measurements establish problematic cost at the bounded entry count.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The feature adds bounded history bookkeeping without per-entry boundary fan-out, extra page requests, or awaited storage I/O.

Scenarios.Scenario: Expand/collapse recent URLs, remove entries, clear workspace history, and replace or close the browser input.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Expand/collapse refreshes the local list and restores focus. Removal/clear mutates memory-backed storage and synchronously refreshes subscribed panes; persistence is deferred. Input replacement/clear disposes input-owned widgets and subscriptions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the final history value or key deletion through existing batched workspace storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one recent-history key mutation per successful remove/clear; target-marker changes share the storage flush. Expansion/collapse performs zero persistence calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These recent-history interactions and their storage mutations did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No persistence await blocks list interaction; only the capped synchronous refresh is on the interaction path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Collapsed view contains at most 3 entries; expanded history contains at most 10, with a 300 px virtual-list viewport. Each explicit remove or clear emits at most one history-change event. Repeated clear/repopulate cycles are confined to the current input's ownership lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: List updates and disposal run synchronously, with no background operation per row. Storage updates use the same throttled, key-coalesced persistence path as navigation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Remove misses cause no save/event. Clear removes the existing workspace key. List templates are reused during splice operations; empty history disposes the active list, and input replacement clears its owning DisposableStore. Toggle Link instances are reused while the input remains attached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in row caps, synchronous refresh, deferred persistence, and input-level cleanup; insufficient evidence of a concrete user-visible performance problem from the disposed-shell edge case.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repeated clear/repopulate cycles can retain disposed widget shells in the input's DisposableStore until input replacement, but no material high-frequency or substantial-growth scenario was established. Normal row counts and active listeners remain small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance finding. Normal interaction work is bounded and virtualized; the inspected cleanup paths do not establish significant long-lived resource growth in the realistic workflows.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Recent URLs Settings from the new overflow menu.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action calls preferencesService.openSettings with an exact setting-ID query, which selects the existing Settings UI path and opens its editor.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One explicit menu invocation and one setting-ID query, independent of recent-history length.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One awaited preferences-editor open per action; no new loop, queue, or parallel request burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: PreferencesService.openSettings2 reuses its cached settings-editor input. The history array is not read, serialized, or traversed by this action.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from tracing the action through openSettings/open/openSettings2 to cached input and group.openEditor; no direct subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is added by the menu/query plumbing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold Settings UI initialization cost is subsystem-dependent, but the diff introduces only an explicit user-requested entry point with no added multiplicity.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression established. This is a demand-driven invocation of the existing settings editor, not eager initialization or repeated work.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the full seven-file inventory and every diff page in the performance-review pass. Traced browser-pane ownership, native navigation/view boundaries, list selection/splicing/disposal, storage memory caching and deferred SQLite persistence, and settings-editor delegation. No high-confidence actionable performance regression or concrete performance-regression fix was found; no findings submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
